relationships.subject: CGRP monoclonal antibodies
relationships.evidence_quote: Patients experienced a marked reduction in migraine frequency, with decreases of −9.87 (95% CI −11.39 to −8.35) migraine days at 3 months

relationships.subject: galcanezumab
relationships.evidence_quote: galcanezumab was associated with a higher likelihood of achieving a ≥ 50% response overall compared with erenumab, regardless of follow-up time

key_findings: In 453 patients, CGRP mAbs gave rapid, sustained reductions in migraine days, acute medication use, disability and mood scores over 12 months, regardless of age.
Galcanezumab had consistently higher odds of >=50% response than erenumab; fremanezumab and eptinezumab were higher at 12 months.
